newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli police to probe corruption allegations.
newsitem.headline: Israeli police to probe corruption allegations.

text.p: Israeli police will probe allegations of high-level corruption which politicians have said could bring down Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government.

The Justice Ministry said the decision to investigate the government's ill-fated appointment of an attorney general was made at a meeting between state prosecutor Enda Arbel and top police officials early on Sunday.

State-owned television caused a furore last week by alleging lawyer Roni Bar-On had promised to arrange a plea bargain for Shas party leader Aryeh Deri, on trial for corruption, in exchange for Deri's support for his appointment as attorney general.

The television also said Deri conditioned his party's support of the Hebron deal with the PLO on Bar-On being appointed attorney general. The 10-member Shas party is one of the pillars of Netanyahu's government coalition.

"The state prosecutor instructed the police to investigate allegations raised in the report on Channel One," said a justice ministry spokeswoman. She said investigators would ask the television to hand over evidence used to prepare the report.
The television has said it will cooperate with police but will not reveal its sources.
